title: When the Summit Burns
premise: Astrid Underhill dives the wreck of the HMS Corvane, a navy vessel sunk under suspicious circumstances, salvaging artifacts she can sell quietly while dodging questions she can't answer. When prospector Elias Vann trades her a map to a wartime cache hidden in the drowned caves of Mount Serapine, she inherits both a fortune and a death sentence: the navy's salvage chief, Commander Reeve, has been hunting the map for years and will burn anyone who holds it. Trapped by the monsoon with a leaking boat and a stranger named Tomas who claims to be Vann's grandson, Astrid must dive the caves before the storms seal them forever. In the end she recovers the cache's true prize—records proving Reeve ordered the Corvane scuttled with its own crew aboard—and must choose between selling her silence and surfacing the truth that will finally let her stop running.
about_author: Astrid Nystrom is a former maritime archaeologist who spent six years cataloguing wrecks across the Coral Sea before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a houseboat in the Andaman Islands, where the monsoon dictates both her schedule and her plots.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She dives the Corvane at dawn, recovering a sealed strongbox while a navy patrol boat circles too close for comfort. We learn she's been moving port to port for three years, haunted by something she saw in the wreck's engine room. Emotional beat: disciplined fear—the routine of a woman who has made invisibility her craft.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In a rain-lashed harbor bar, prospector Elias Vann, coughing blood, offers her a waterproofed map to the Serapine caves in exchange for one promise: that whatever she finds, she tells the truth about it. Hours later she watches men burn Vann's shack. Emotional beat: the trap closing—she took the promise before she understood its cost.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas intercepts Astrid at her boat, claiming Vann was his grandfather and that the map is his inheritance. He knows too much about the Corvane to be innocent, but he also saves her from a dockside ambush. Emotional beat: wary alliance—two people who trust no one deciding, provisionally, to trust each other.

chapters.title: Commander Reeve
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV. The navy's salvage chief interrogates a harbor informant and reveals his obsession: he was the Corvane's junior officer, and he's spent decades ensuring the truth of the scuttling stays drowned. He orders Astrid's boat flagged. Emotional beat: cold menace—Reeve believes he is the story's hero, protecting an institution at any price.

chapters.title: Leaking Toward Serapine
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid and Tomas run for the mountain through the monsoon's edge; the boat's hull cracks and they bail by hand through the night. Tomas reveals fragments of Vann's past—and that the old man didn't just find the cache, he was hired to hide it. Emotional beat: grudging intimacy forged in shared danger.

chapters.title: What the Engine Room Held
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with a flashback. Sheltering in a cove, Astrid finally tells Tomas what she saw three years ago: crew remains chained below decks when the Corvane went down—men who were never meant to escape. Emotional beat: confession and relief; her secret, spoken aloud, becomes a shared burden instead of a solitary one.

chapters.title: The Drowned Caves
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. They reach Serapine and make the first cave dive through a flooded lava tube. Inside: crates of naval records, gold, and evidence that Vann was paid by the crew's own families, not the navy, to preserve the proof. Reeve's divers arrive above. Emotional beat: awe curdling to dread—the treasure is the truth, and the truth is hunted.

chapters.title: Cut Off
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Reeve's men trap them in the caves as the monsoon hits full force; Tomas takes a bullet covering Astrid's escape through a secondary passage, and she must leave him with the records while she surfaces alone. Emotional beat: sacrifice and guilt—the promise to Vann now weighs more than her own survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Summit Burns
chapters.summary: Climax. Astrid's POV. Reeve torches the mountain camp to destroy the evidence and force Astrid out; she uses the fire's chaos to trigger an emergency beacon from the Corvane's recovered strongbox, broadcasting the records' coordinates to every ship in the strait. Confronted publicly, Reeve falters. Emotional beat: desperate courage—turning her invisibility inside out to become the one witness he can't erase.

chapters.title: Surface
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, weeks later. Tomas survives; the inquiry opens; the Corvane's dead get names in the record. Astrid sells the boat, buys a slower one, and—for the first time in years—stays in one port through a whole season. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—she learns that survival was never the price; forgetting was, and she's done paying it.
